posts.title: Clydebuilt Refreshes Its Range With Three 10-Year-Old Malts
posts.excerpt: Clydebuilt's refreshed Scotch range pairs two sherry-matured expressions with the American-oak-aged Candlebrae, in new River Clyde packaging.
posts.meta_description: Explore Clydebuilt's refreshed 10-year-old Scotch range: two sherry-matured malts and American-oak Candlebrae, with new River Clyde packaging.
posts.selection_note: An uncovered 6 October producer announcement with specific expressions and maturation details; the article separates the bottling range from Ardgowan's own young spirit.
posts.content:
Clydebuilt has refreshed its Scotch whisky range with two sherry-matured 10-year-olds and a limited Highland malt aged in American oak. Ardgowan Distillery's 6 October 2026 announcement also introduces bottles and giftboxes carrying a map of the River Clyde.

Three Expressions, Different Strengths

The core range comprises Clydebuilt 10 Years Old Sherry Cask Matured at 46% ABV and its 100 Proof counterpart at 57.1%. The limited Clydebuilt 10 Years Old Candlebrae is bottled at 48%. Whisky Maker Laura Davies developed all three expressions.

Sherry Casks Or American Oak?

The Sherry Cask Matured product page identifies a Speyside malt aged in sherry butts and European oak Pedro Ximenez and Oloroso hogsheads from Jose y Miguel Martin. The producer describes dried fruit and almonds on the nose, then honey, raisins, cinnamon and cloves.

Candlebrae takes a different route: a Highland single malt matured for a decade in American oak. Its producer notes include baked apple, waxy citrus, apricot, cream and spiced oak. Both product pages specify no added colouring or chill filtration.

The Brand And The Distillery

Clydebuilt is an independent-bottling range launched in 2019. Its brand home, Ardgowan, began distilling its own spirit in June 2025. These 10-year-old bottlings belong to the Clydebuilt range, not a decade of whisky production at that new distillery.

Choosing A First Pour

Our suggestion is to compare the cask profiles before choosing by strength. Try a small neat pour in a tulip-shaped glass; add water gradually if preferred. For the fruit-and-spice style, roasted almonds or a little dark chocolate are useful pairing ideas.

posts.title: How Long Does Wine Last After Opening? A Home Storage Guide
posts.excerpt: Reclose and refrigerate opened wine, including reds. Learn realistic freshness windows, sparkling-wine stoppers and a simple routine for the next pour.
posts.meta_title: How Long Does Opened Wine Last? Storage Guide | BevOry
posts.meta_description: Learn how to store opened red, white and sparkling wine, why a fridge helps, and when to use a Champagne stopper. Practical advice from BevOry.
posts.selection_note: An everyday storage query distinct from the decanting guide; the copy treats freshness windows as quality guidance and uses the Champagne authority's bottle-specific advice.
posts.content:
Reclose an opened bottle of still wine and put it in the fridge, including red wine. WSET's preservation guide says a reclosed red or white can stay relatively fresh for up to five days when refrigerated. That is a useful planning window, not a promise that every bottle will taste unchanged until day five.

Air And Heat Change The Wine

Opening exposes wine to oxygen, while heat and light also work against freshness. WSET recommends closing the bottle after pouring, keeping it upright and refrigerating it. Cooler storage slows oxidation; standing an opened bottle upright reduces the surface exposed to air.

Our practical routine is to write the opening date on a removable label and return the bottle to the fridge after serving. In a warm Indian kitchen, the counter is not a substitute for cool storage.

Red Wine Can Go In The Fridge

Storage temperature and serving temperature are different decisions. You can keep the remaining red cold and let the next small pour warm before drinking. WSET's wine-myth guide places red-wine serving temperatures broadly at 13-18 degrees C and notes that lighter reds can be enjoyable chilled.

Our suggestion is to adjust the glass rather than leave the whole bottle out throughout dinner. Take another taste as it warms and choose the temperature you prefer.

Sparkling Wine Needs Its Own Stopper

The Comite Champagne FAQ says an opened Champagne bottle can be kept for one or two days when immediately closed with a special airtight stopper. Its guidance describes a seal held securely against the bottle neck by latches.

Use a stopper designed for sparkling wine and refrigerate the bottle. WSET's wine-myth guide also rejects the familiar spoon-in-the-neck trick. Set the proper stopper beside the glasses before opening Champagne or Prosecco, so it is ready after the first pour.

Plan For The Next Glass

Plan the next serving before returning the bottle to the fridge. Treat the day count as a guide to freshness, not a universal shelf-life guarantee, and avoid tasting a bottle merely to investigate suspected contamination.

posts.title: Bringing Alcohol From Gurugram To Delhi: The One-Litre Rule
posts.excerpt: Delhi's published excise rules list a one-litre limit when entering from another state. Bottle count and Metro travel do not replace that volume limit.
posts.meta_title: Alcohol From Gurugram to Delhi: Carrying Rules | BevOry
posts.meta_description: Bringing alcohol from Gurugram or Noida into Delhi? Understand the published one-litre limit, bottle-size examples and Delhi Metro rules on BevOry.
posts.selection_note: A specific NCR travel question, supported by Delhi's published rules, its excise FAQ and DMRC's current state-law notice rather than a blanket two-bottle claim.
posts.content:
Delhi's published excise rules list a one-litre limit for Indian or foreign liquor when entering Delhi from another state. That is the relevant quantity provision to read before bringing a purchase from Gurugram or Noida into Delhi. It is a volume limit, not a universal allowance of one or two bottles.

Where The One-Litre Figure Comes From

Rule 20 of the Delhi Excise Rules, 2010 sets out the quantity table for individuals aged 25 or older. The table lists one litre while entering Delhi from other states. The department's FAQ, question 12, repeats that figure separately from its domestic-possession quantities.

Rule 3 addresses private consumption, not resale, within the prescribed maximum quantities. Do not turn that private-consumption provision into permission to move stock for a business.

Count Millilitres, Not Bottles

Two 750 ml bottles total 1,500 ml, which exceeds one litre. Two 500 ml bottles total 1,000 ml. These examples explain the arithmetic; they are not a guarantee of permission for a particular journey.

Compare the net volume shown on each bottle and add the quantities together. A lower price, a sealed carton or a different mode of travel does not change the total liquid volume.

Delhi Metro Does Not Override State Rules

DMRC's published prohibited-items notice explicitly says the concerned state's excise rules and restrictions apply to alcohol carriage. Do not treat a Metro bottle-count allowance as an exemption from Delhi's interstate quantity provision.

Check The Direction Of Your Journey

This guide concerns entering Delhi. It does not set the rules for a return trip into Haryana or Uttar Pradesh, nor does it cover commercial supply. For permit questions or an unusual journey, seek guidance from the relevant excise department before travelling.

Keep any purchase documentation available, but do not treat a receipt as permission to exceed a quantity restriction. Compare city prices on BevOry with the intended purchase location in mind; a price difference is not a transport authorisation.
